page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors utilizing the 64-bit ARM64 Neoverse-N1 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

This instance is highly optimized for networking, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48,563.42 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,689.0. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached reads at 1,894.04 GB/sec, though uncached large-block writes drop to 74.98 GB/sec. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 973.0 and a weak rating in single-threaded gzip compression.

The c6gn.8xlarge is designed for network-intensive, compute-heavy workloads. It demonstrates solid capabilities in multi-threaded tasks, such as software compilation with a Geekbench clang score of 25,637.0 and static web serving at 33.08 GB/sec throughput. The ARM64 architecture offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out workloads compared to traditional x86 architectures, though it lacks specialized instruction sets like AVX or AMX. It is highly suited for high-performance computing, network appliances, and distributed data processing.
